newsitem.title: USA: American Home unit seeks vaccine approval.
newsitem.headline: American Home unit seeks vaccine approval.

text.p: Wyeth-Ayerst Laboratories said on Friday its Wyeth-Lederle Vaccines and Pediatrics unit has filed a New Product License Application with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration seeking approval for use of Wyeth's Tetracel vaccine for childhood illnesses.
Wyeth-Ayerst is the pharmaceutical division of American Home Products Corp.

The company said the FDA has accepted the application for review. The new vaccine is intended to protect toddlers 12 months old to 18 months from diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis and Haemophilus influenzae.
As a combination vaccine, Tetracel could reduce by half the number of injections children now receive, Wyeth said.
In its two clinical trials, Tetracel performed well, the company said.
